findings.explanation: license_usage.log is written by splunkd on the license manager itself and indexed into `_internal` with no forwarder input, modular input or poll; it is only complete on the license manager (or wherever the license manager's `_internal` is forwarded). The same wrong mechanism appears in `app` and in `detailedImplementation` ('Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into _internal').
findings.quote: `index=_internal` `source=*license_usage.log*` `type=Usage` Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: license_usage.log (`index=_internal source=*license_usage.log* type=Usage`, sourcetype `splunkd`) generated by the license manager; run the search on the license manager or Monitoring Console, or forward the license manager's internal logs to the indexing tier. No add-on required.

findings.explanation: Each `type=Usage` event already carries `poolsz` (the pool quota in bytes), and `type=RolloverSummary` events carry `stack` and `stacksz`; a hand-maintained lookup duplicates these and goes stale after license renewals or pool changes.
findings.quote: (1) Build `splunk_license_quota` from your entitlement and stacking plan (GB per day per pool).
findings.suggested_fix: Use `poolsz` from the Usage events for pool quota (`max(poolsz)` per pool per day) and `type=RolloverSummary` with `stack`/`stacksz` for stack-level daily totals; keep a lookup only for overrides such as internal chargeback targets.

findings.explanation: `implementation` promises a two-consecutive-day rule, but the SPL returns every pool-day above 85% across the last 30 days with no streak logic, so a single old spike re-alerts daily for a month. The detailedImplementation's 'Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h' contradicts the SPL's own `earliest=-30d`.
findings.quote: (2) Alert at eighty-five percent for two consecutive days.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the rule the SPL actually implements (any day in the window above 85% of quota), or state that a streak check (e.g. streamstats over the last two complete days) is needed; schedule once daily shortly after license-manager midnight with a window matching the logic.

findings.explanation: Data model acceleration has nothing to do with license consumption or finding noisy sources (summaries are not counted against license), and `detailedImplementation` adds 'Enable Data Model Acceleration ... otherwise tstats/mstats may return no results' although the SPL uses neither.
findings.quote: (3) Pair with `data model` acceleration and sourcetype-level volume reports to find noisy sources.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with: drill into the offending pool by `idx` and `st` (sourcetype) from the same Usage events, or use the Monitoring Console License Usage 'Previous 30 days' view split by sourcetype/index. Remove the DMA paragraph.

findings.explanation: The scenarios use placeholder sourcetypes and generic causes (synthetic probes, maintenance windows) that do not apply to license data. Real benign causes of a high pool-day are missing.
findings.quote: **Batch `sum` on `configured_sourcetype`** — Scheduled automation elevates `pool` without crossing `util_pct` > 85
findings.suggested_fix: List license-specific causes: planned historical backfills or re-ingest, a newly onboarded source during an approved project, duplicate forwarding during a migration, `b` values squashed into one pool after a pool reassignment, and day boundaries computed in the search-head timezone rather than the license manager's midnight rollover.

findings.explanation: Validation against a cloud billing console, a 'vendor admin UI inventory count' and HEC/API-error troubleshooting do not apply to Splunk license data.
findings.quote:
Step 3 — Validate
compare with the cloud billing console for the same scope, accounts, and time range.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate by comparing the daily per-pool totals with Settings > Licensing (license manager) or Monitoring Console > Indexing > License Usage for the same day.

findings.explanation: Splunk Cloud Platform customers do not manage license pools or stacks, and the repository guide notes workload pricing in Cloud and changes to volume license pools in 10.x, so the pool/stack logic may not apply on Cloud.
findings.suggested_fix: Check whether Splunk Cloud exposes pool-level `type=Usage` data to customers and whether pools exist on workload-priced stacks; if not, scope splunkVersions to Splunk Enterprise and point Cloud users to the Cloud Monitoring Console license/entitlement views.

findings.explanation: HEC and inputs.conf are unrelated to license_usage.log; the license usage documentation is missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Reference the Splunk Enterprise Admin manual pages on license usage reporting / license_usage.log and the Monitoring Console license usage dashboards.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `type=Usage` events carry `pool` and `poolsz` but no `stack` field (stack appears on `type=RolloverSummary`), so `stats sum(gb) by _time, pool, stack` drops every event and returns no rows. Group by pool only and use `poolsz` for quota, or use RolloverSummary for stack totals. Evidence: https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/observability/splunk-platform/splunk-enterprise/5/SPLK051238-create-a-report-based-on-licence-usage-log.html
Title promises 'Stack Warnings' but the SPL never reads license warnings/violations (e.g. licenser messages); either add that source or retitle to pool usage versus quota.

summary: The goal (daily license pool usage versus quota) is a good fit for license_usage.log, but the text misstates where the data comes from (Universal Forwarder), asks the reader to hand-build a quota lookup although `poolsz` is already in every Usage event, pairs the UC with irrelevant data-model acceleration, and promises a two-consecutive-day rule and 'stack warnings' that the SPL does not implement; the SPL also groups by a `stack` field that Usage events do not carry.
